address: Apollolaan 4 / Stadionweg 5 (Apollohal), Amsterdam-Zuid (Olympisch Kwartier): 1934 sports hall of brick with a tall glazed upper hall, a curved glass roof edge, brick entrance annexes with round windows and a canopied glass entrance
notes: Apollolaan 4 / Stadionweg 5 (BAG pand 0363100012134507, built 1934, 98 3DBAG wall surfaces, roof max 14.5 m): the Apollohal, the 1934 sports hall of the Olympic quarter in Amsterdam-Zuid: a long brick hall with a glazed clerestory and a curved glass roof edge, flanked by two-storey brick annexes with round windows and a canopied glass entrance on the Stadionweg side. Photographed: the long south-west flank (w01-231, 2017-04-19), the north-west annexes and glazed gable (w04-321 and w05-321, 2020-05-13) and the glazed entrance (w06-231, 2024-11-05); w02-51 and w03-51 have no panorama within 35 m.

walls[0] = panel 22 (SW, 66.6 m, eaves 11.9): a blank brick plinth under two glazed bands, drawn as 3 storeys with a blank ground and 22 bays of wide windows without sills. walls[1] = panels 21, 13 and 17 (NW, 11 m, 10 m and 9 m, eaves 6.3): the two-storey brick annex fronts with white-framed windows, 2 storeys x 3 bays. walls[2] = panel 14 (NW, 35.7 m, eaves 12.1 over a 6.8 m base): the glazed gable of the hall above the annexes, drawn as a one-storey curtain wall with mullions and transoms, with APOLLOHAL on a name band (the photographed letters are on the glass). walls[3] = panel 31 (SW end, 9.8 m, eaves 3.6): the glazed entrance under a flat canopy, one storey with a glazed ground and an entrance with canopy in bay 1.

Simplified: the glass gable is a flat curtain wall (the photographed hall edge is curved), the clerestory on the long flank is wide windows over a blank base, the entrance is a canopy and a glazed door set in three bays, the round windows of the annexes are not modelled and stay plain wall. Not drawn: the south-east end wall, the north-east long wall (panels 63, 44, 26, no panorama) and the low service range on the north-east, which stay blank brick.

Re-fit 2026-10-14 (kit vocabulary lane) from w01-231: walls[0] is a glazed-hall, a tan-grey brick base to 0.4 of the eaves (photo 0.40) under one glass skin to the eaves with a mullion grid of 26 lights per structural bay (0.64 m; photo 0.63 m) and 6 rows (photo 6, about 1.03 m), structural posts every 16.6 m (photo about 15.1 m: 4 bays over 66.6 m), dark grey-blue glass #46545c (photo raw #596b74 with the sky reflected; darkened to the dark band the user reads) and a pale tan plinth #a2937e (photo raw #5c5347 under overcast, x1.75 by the light metal door panel).
